Thanks again for your time this morning — great conversation. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned before the pilot kickoff:

Summary of what we agreed
- Pilot scope: invoice extraction + customer-match reranker (embeddings) for 3k monthly documents.
- Success criteria: >95% schema-validated extractions for top-3 fields, end-to-end latency <= 400ms per request p50.
- Must-haves: private API keys with rotation, region routing to us-west, and an SDK-based validator for the JSON contract.

Integration checklist (items we can start in parallel)
1) SDK onboarding: we'll provide Python/Node quickstart and a small test harness. Please confirm dev language preference.
2) Auth: token-based keys with recommended rotation policy (see attached auth diagram). Option to integrate your KMS for key storage.
3) Output contract: we attached an initial schema-sample.json as a starting point. We recommend a two-step validation: model-constrained decoding hints + SDK-side JSON schema validation and retry on failure.
4) Routing & capacity: you mentioned steady QPS ~10 with occasional spikes to 50. We'll configure a dedicated routing profile to prefer low-latency instances in us-west and fallback to a compatible quantized variant if capacity is constrained.
5) Embeddings & reranker: we'll provide an embeddings pipeline and a reranker prototype; need a representative dataset for tuning.

Open questions for you
- Which language should we prioritize for the SDK quickstart (Python, Node, Go)?
- Any data residency constraints beyond us-west?
- Will your security team require an NDA/PO before we send sample logs for the pilot?

Attachments referenced: [regenflow-mvp-reqs.pdf (PDF)] [schema-sample.json (JSON)]

Proposed timeline
- This week: exchange sample data + confirm SDK language and auth pattern
- Next week: SE-run onboarding, shared sandbox keys, and first validation run

If that captures it, please reply with the language preference and whether your security team needs an NDA before we ship the test bundle. I’ll loop in Dev and Tessa for scheduling once you confirm.

Best,

Hi Samantha — quick technical answers and a recommended pattern based on similar pilots:

1) SDK support: official SDKs for Python and Node; community Go client available. The SDK supports automatic token refresh if you provide a rotation endpoint or integrate a KMS-backed secret provider.

2) Auth model: recommended pattern is short-lived API keys (1h) stored in your KMS. SDK will call your rotation endpoint to fetch and cache tokens; we do not store long-lived secrets in our platform for private deployments. See attached auth-flow-diagram.png.

3) Constrained decoding & validation strategy (recommended)
- Use constrained decoding hints (e.g., strong system prompt + schema-aware sampling: temperature=0 to reduce entropy + max_tokens tuned).
- Model returns a candidate JSON string. SDK runs a local JSON Schema validation. If validation fails, SDK will do up to 2 automated retries with adjusted decoding hints (lower temperature, narrower token sampling, extra clarifying prompt).
- If still invalid, SDK either: 1) fallback to a safe default payload and mark extraction as failed, or 2) fail-fast and return the raw output to your validation queue depending on your chosen policy. We'll configure this per-route.

Example pseudo-flow:
- call model with prompt + schema hint
- response -> sdk.validate(response, schema)
- if valid -> accept
- else -> retry with temperature=0, add 'return strictly this JSON' prompt (up to 2 times)
- if still invalid -> route to manual review or fallback payload

4) Cost guardrails: SDK enforces a max retry budget per request and tracks token spend. We'll set a default cap (e.g., 2 retries / request) and surface alerts when the budget is exceeded.

5) Embeddings/reranker: we recommend pre-computing embeddings in batches and using a hybrid reranker: sparse + dense. For pilot, we can tune on your sample set; send 200-500 representative examples.

Attaching the auth flow diagram and a small sample schema you can iterate on. Happy to do a short hands-on SDK session — suggest Wed or Thu next week.

—Karthik
